# The Box: full machine reference for agents

This is the complete reference for provisioning and managing a Box programmatically.
For the short runbook, see https://thebox.build/llms.txt

The Box is a self-managing appliance OS. One generic image installs any machine;
per-machine identity (hostname, keys, pairing code, disk layout) arrives at first
boot as an "orders" handoff. Every change (a service, a platform update) is built
into a new atomic Nix generation and switched to with a health check; any generation
can be rolled back. There is no central controller and no phone-home: a Box trusts
its operator (you) and the keys/codes you hand it, never another machine.

Management endpoints all live on TCP port 2693.


## 1. Orders (box-install.json)

The install handoff. JSON. Fields:

- erase_disk (bool, REQUIRED): explicit consent to wipe the target disk. The
  installer refuses to touch any disk unless this is true.
- hostname (string): the new Box's hostname. "auto" (default) derives a stable
  per-machine name, which is what you want for batch/agent installs.
- ssh_authorized_keys (array of string): SSH public keys authorized on the Box
  (user `murphy`, passwordless sudo). Put the agent's/operator's public key here
  so you can SSH back in after takeover.
- enrollment_code_hash (string): lowercase hex SHA-256 of a one-time pairing
  code. Seeded into the Box's auth store at first boot so the Box is pairable
  from first boot with no SSH: redeem the plaintext code (§4) for a session token.
- wifi (object, optional): { "ssid": "...", "password": "..." } for Wi-Fi.
- static_ip (object, optional): { "address": "192.168.1.50/24", "gateway":
  "192.168.1.1", "dns": ["1.1.1.1"] } pins the LAN address at first boot.
  Only "address" (IPv4 with prefix) is required; DNS defaults to the gateway.
  Applies to the Wi-Fi connection when wifi is set, otherwise to wired.
  Default: DHCP.
- storage (object, optional): { "layout": "single" | "mirror" | "pool",
  "min_disk_gb": N }. Default: single, largest internal disk. You may instead set
  "disk": "/dev/disk/by-id/..." to name an explicit device.
- cloudflare_tunnel_token (string, optional): a Cloudflare Tunnel token to bring
  up public access at first boot.

Minimal orders for an agent provision:

    { "erase_disk": true,
      "hostname": "auto",
      "ssh_authorized_keys": ["ssh-ed25519 AAAA... agent@host"],
      "enrollment_code_hash": "<sha256 of your one-time code>" }


### Authority note

`tools/list` on your Box is the authority for what tools exist and their
schemas; this file documents the common core, not all of them. Port 2693 in
examples is the DEFAULT management port - substitute your Box's actual port
everywhere. Destructive tools (delete_service, backup_restore,
provision_machine) QUEUE for a human tap on the console's Approvals page
unless your session was granted autonomy: you get {"pending_approval": id}
back - poll approval_status with that id, and do not re-submit. Platform
updates ARE driven over MCP: channel_check reports, channel_update applies
(it delegates the switch to the Box's root updater; pass force:true only when
channel_check tells you to).

## 2. The installer (install.sh)

https://thebox.build/install.sh is an x86_64 in-place takeover. It fetches the
Box netboot kernel+initrd, stages your orders in RAM, and kexecs straight into
the Box installer, which wipes the disk and installs NixOS as a Box. No USB, no
reboot menu. Orders never touch the disk (they ride in RAM across the kexec).

Supply orders one of two ways:

- BOX_ORDERS_B64=<base64 of box-install.json>  (env var, the normal agent path)
- BOX_ORDERS=/path/to/box-install.json         (a file on the target)

Run as root, or via sudo. Examples:

    # over SSH, orders embedded (no file on the target):
    ssh root@TARGET "curl -fsSL https://thebox.build/install.sh | sudo BOX_ORDERS_B64=$B64 sh"

The installer kexecs near the end, so an SSH invocation's connection will drop.
That is success, not failure. The authoritative "it worked" signal is the Box
answering on port 2693 (§3).

Bare metal with no OS (blank disk) cannot be reached by SSH, so there is nothing to
run install.sh. A human flashes the SD/USB image or netboots the installer once
(https://thebox.build/docs/install.html#bare-metal , and for Raspberry Pi,
https://thebox.build/docs/raspberry-pi.html). From there the machine is agent-
drivable on the LAN (see §2b). Once it is a Box, everything from §3 on applies
unchanged.


## 2b. The installer beacon (bare-metal, no SSH)

A machine sitting in the installer's setup wizard advertises itself over mDNS so
an agent can discover and finish it without a screen: the LAN-native analog of
SSH. This is how you provision a machine that has no OS to SSH into.

Discovery: it advertises the DNS-SD service type `_thebox-setup._tcp` on port
2693, with TXT records vendor=thebox, role=installer, state=unclaimed,
pin=required. Browse for it and read the address from the record:

    avahi-browse -rpt _thebox-setup._tcp | grep '^=' | grep IPv4
    # (or: dns-sd -B _thebox-setup._tcp)

Identity: GET http://IP:2693/api/hello (unauthenticated). Returns
{ "thebox":"installer", "role":"installer", "state":"unclaimed"|"installing"|"done",
"pin_required":bool, "port":2693, "version":"..." }. Use it to confirm you found a
Box installer and whether a setup PIN is needed, before touching anything.

Setup PIN: the destructive endpoints are gated by a PIN presented in the
`X-Setup-Pin` header. The PIN is shown on the machine's own screen, or set in the
Configurator (rides in as `setup_pin`); you supply it out of band. This is the
physical-security gate (the pre-install analog of the enrollment code), so a
random host on the LAN can't claim a booting machine with its own keys.

The setup API (all under http://IP:2693, all PIN-gated except /api/hello):
- GET  /api/probe  → { ok, disks:[{path,size_bytes,model,rotational,removable,...}] }
- POST /api/plan   { "layout": "single"|"mirror"|"pool" } → resolved layout preview
- POST /api/commit { "layout": "...", "base": <orders> } → writes the effective
  orders + disko config and starts the install. `base` is the orders object from
  §1 (hostname, ssh_authorized_keys, enrollment_code_hash, wifi); the chosen
  layout is merged into it. This is the commit. It wipes and installs.
- GET  /api/status → { committed, done, log } (install progress)

Agent flow: browse → /api/hello → (build orders as in §1) → POST /api/commit with
the PIN → poll /api/status until done (or just wait for the Box on 2693, §3) →
redeem your pairing code (§4) → manage over MCP (§6). The beacon stops advertising
the moment setup commits.

`boxd provision <ssh-target>` packages the whole §1–§4 flow (orders, ssh+install,
wait, redeem) into one command; add --json for `{address, token, mcp_url,
dashboard}`. Flags: --hostname, --ssh-key (repeatable; literal key or .pub path),
--layout single|mirror|pool, --reach-host, --ssh-opt, --install-url, --boot-timeout.


## 3. Readiness

GET http://BOX:2693/api/v1/health is public (no auth) and returns a coarse-health
JSON object once boxd is up. Poll it to know the Box has finished installing and
booting:

    until curl -fsS http://BOX:2693/api/v1/health >/dev/null; do sleep 5; done


## 4. Pairing: get a session token

POST http://BOX:2693/pair/redeem (public path). Body: form-encoded
`code=<code>&label=<who>` OR JSON `{"code":"...","label":"..."}` - both work;
`label` names the session in the console's device list. The one-time code is
consumed on use (single-use; replays fail).

- With `Accept: application/json` → responds `{"token":"...","label":"agent"}`.
  Use the token as a Bearer credential (§5). This is the agent path.
- Without it (a browser) → sets the `box_session` cookie and redirects.

    TOKEN=$(curl -fsS -X POST http://BOX:2693/pair/redeem \
      -H 'accept: application/json' --data-urlencode "code=$CODE" | jq -r .token)

Where codes come from: (a) the enrollment_code_hash you put in the orders (you
know the plaintext); (b) the recovery kit printed at install; (c) on an existing
Box, `boxd auth mint --label agent` prints a session token directly, and
"add device" mints a fresh one-time code from an already-paired session.


## 5. Authentication

Every management request (everything except §3 health, deployed public sites, the
pairing flow, and the favicon) requires a valid session, supplied as either:

- Authorization: Bearer <token>     (agents)
- Cookie: box_session=<token>       (browsers)

Loopback-as-the-Box-sees-it, non-proxied requests (an SSH -L tunnel
terminating ON the Box) are trusted
without a token. Tokens are stored SHA-256-hashed; each is a named "device" the
operator can list and revoke.


## 6. MCP server

POST http://BOX:2693/mcp is JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP, authenticated as in §5.
Stateless (no SSE session required). Standard methods:

- initialize → returns protocolVersion + serverInfo {name:"the-box"}.
- notifications/initialized → acknowledged (HTTP 202, no body).
- tools/list → { tools: [...] }.
- tools/call → { name, arguments } → result. Tool-level failures come back as a
  result with "isError": true. (Missing/invalid ARGUMENTS are the exception:
  those are JSON-RPC -32602 protocol errors, per spec.)

Envelope example (list tools):

    {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}

Call example (deploy):

    {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{
      "name":"deploy_static_site",
      "arguments":{"name":"welcome","index_html":"<h1>hi</h1>"}}}

### Tools

Deploy / change (each activates a new atomic generation):

- deploy_static_site: create/update a static site. args: name (required; 1-32
  chars a-z 0-9 '-', not starting or ending with '-'), index_html (single-page HTML) OR source_path (a directory
  on the Box to copy as the site root), domain (optional public domain for tunnel
  traffic, e.g. site.example.com).
- deploy: create/update a service from any template. args: name (required),
  template (required; an id from list_templates, e.g. "static-site"), params
  (object; template-specific), domain (optional), public (bool, optional).
- delete_service: remove a service. args: name (required). Previous generation
  stays available for rollback.
- rollback: switch back to a previous generation. args: generation (required,
  number from list_generations).

Inspect (read-only):

- get_status: active generation, declared services, build backend.
- list_services: services with template, domain, URL, active state.
- list_templates: deployable templates (id, title, description). Call before
  `deploy` to get valid template ids and their params.
- list_generations: all generations, newest last, current one marked.
- list_history: git history of the Box's declarative config, newest first.
- channel_status: running platform release, configured channel, pinned revision.
- channel_check: whether a newer platform than the pinned one is available.
  (Applying an update is done by the Box's root updater, not via MCP.)

Backups:

- backup_status: destination reachability, snapshot count, last-run time.
- backup_snapshots: list snapshots (id, time, paths), newest last.
- backup_now: take a snapshot now (e.g. before a risky change); blocks until done.
- backup_restore: restore in place (DESTRUCTIVE). args: snapshot ("latest"
  default), scope ("config" default | "all" | a service name).

A typical agent session: initialize → list_templates → deploy/deploy_static_site
→ get_status/list_services to confirm → (backup_now before risky changes) →
rollback if needed.


## 7. Ports & networking

- 2693/tcp: dashboard, JSON API (/api/v1), MCP (/mcp), pairing (/pair).
- 22/tcp: SSH (keys from ssh_authorized_keys). Loopback HTTP is trusted, so an
  SSH tunnel to 2693 reaches management without a token.
- Deployed services with a domain are served publicly via a tunnel (Box Connect
  or a BYO Cloudflare tunnel), routed by Host header. The dashboard is never
  reachable through a service domain.


## 8. Trust model

A Box trusts its operator, not other machines. Sessions are per-Box and revocable.
Give each agent its own SSH key and its own session token so it can be retired
independently. No account, no phone-home; keys, pairing codes, and the backup key
are generated on the Box or by you and never leave it. Backups are client-side
encrypted, so storage providers only ever hold ciphertext.
